We introduce a Temporal Difference (TD) learning approach designed to enable robots to navigate marine areas by predicting the one-step gradient of the Value function. This method estimates the gradient using only scalar rewards received during interactions, making it an exemplar of model-free reinforcement learning. The regression process employs a Gaussian Process, which offers flexible function approximations and provides uncertainty estimates alongside predictions. This capability allows the system to prioritize unvisited regions with high uncertainty for exploration. The article also examines the computational overhead associated with rendering uncertainty maps over grid-based representations of the environment. Experimental results involve both a simulation platform and physical hardware—a mobile robot utilizing the Robot Operating System (ROS)—to validate the proposed methodology.

"This survey explores recent findings regarding complex quadrics and isothermic surfaces, with a primary focus on developing a simplified approach to classify doubly ruled quadrics. Additionally, it introduces a specific type of metric on the space of isothermic surfaces involving their Hopf differentials. By taking the limit of the resulting metric when the surface approaches a lightcone in the Grassmannian of lines on the quadrics, a new class of metrics over the space of dual lightcone quadrics is obtained, which in turn defines an infinite class of metrics over the space of rank-three signature (-++). Applications include using the resulting lightcone quadrics metrics to solve the initial value problem for the metric on Lorentzian surfaces."

We examine the synthesis of the $L^2$-operator associated with $\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon X \mid \mathcal{G}]$, where $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mu)$ represents a probability space, $\mathcal{G}$ is a sub-$\sigma$-algebra, and $(X,\varepsilon)$ are independent, square-integrable random variables where $\varepsilon$ is Rademacher. The analysis focuses on approximation via Hilbert-Schmidt operators using the $L^2$-tensor product spaces formed by $L^2(\mu)$ and a given $L^2$-tensor product structure. Results demonstrate consistent lower bounds for this approximation strategy, highlighting that even with Hilbert-Schmidt operators, the operator cannot generally be uniformly well-approximated. Conversely, when the conditional expectation takes the form $\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon X \mid \mathcal{G}] = \mathbb{E}[\varepsilon] \cdot \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{G}}$, uniform lower bounds hold. These findings are pivotal for quantifying the efficacy of randomized smoothing within classification and regression tasks in machine learning.

While incorporating temporal elements into knowledge graph embeddings (TKEs) has historically improved the embedding quality and performance of downstream tasks, the mechanisms behind this enhancement remain obscure. This study provides a thorough investigation into this phenomenon. We evaluate the effectiveness of different temporal representation strategies across a range of scenarios, including various embedding models, time-aware representations, and temporal learning algorithms. Our experimental results lead to the following conclusions: (1) the performance uplift offered by TKEs over standard KG embeddings is gradually diminishing; (2) the observed performance gain is exclusively driven by training on ground truth data rather than providing superior representation for both true and validation triples; (3) integrating temporal information yields negligible or invalid enhancements when applied to datasets of low size or when assessing entities exhibiting high temporal consistency. These insights carry significant implications for the practical deployment of TKEs.

This research paper addresses a query initially raised by Evans concerning graph C*-algebras. We establish that the strong shift equivalence (SSE) of row-finite graphs corresponds precisely to the Morita equivalence of their associated C*-algebras. Consequently, any graph invariant derivable from the C*-algebra's structure can be directly transferred to the level of the underlying graphs. As a significant application, we provide a novel proof of Brown-Pimentel's theorem, demonstrating that two Taylor Q-algebras are Morita equivalent if and only if their underlying graphs are strongly shift equivalent. Furthermore, we investigate properties involving free tail-tadad equivalence and its connection to unitary equivalence freeness, along with defining and analyzing the concept of algebraic tail-tadad equivalence at the algebraic structure of row-finite graphs.

This study examines the imaginary component of the heavy quark potential along with the concept of heavy quarkonium dissociation in a thermal environment with strong magnetic fields. Our findings indicate that a magnetic field intensifies the dissociation probability of heavy quarkonium states. Specifically, the effect becomes most pronounced when the field strength aligns with thermal scales; under these conditions, the dissociation temperature can decrease by approximately 20% due to a significant increase in the rate of quark-antiquark pair separation.

Addressing open-domain questions demands extensive world knowledge exceeding what any pre-trained Language Model (LM) can hold alone, necessitating external help. While prior research explores integrating external knowledge (e.g., Knowledge Graphs) via retrieval and guidance or post-generation verification, these methods often yield suboptimal performance. To improve retrieval accuracy, we introduce an innovative hybrid architecture combining a decoder-less Retrieval LM with a verifier to mutually enhance one another. Leveraging the verifier allows our retrieval process to focus solely on critical reasoning without being constrained by standard retrieval LM constraints. Experiments on three benchmarks across two major knowledge resources confirm our method outperforms state-of-the-art systems. Source code is accessible at https://github.com/HKU-AI-Research/OPENLM.

We introduce a fresh construction for high-dimensional expanders, which serve as an extension of expander graphs to higher dimensions. Building on the framework of coset geometric constructions found in geometric expander graphs, our approach defines a hypergraph where vertices correspond to the vertices of a simplicial complex, and its connecting structure is governed by the isomorphism types of the links of individual simplices. To enable expansion through such high-dimensional structures, we establish necessary conditions requiring specific connectivity within the vertices of these associated links. We demonstrate that graphs built from simple complexes using this method exhibit high-dimensional expansion properties. Furthermore, we prove that high-dimensional expanders are robust against vertex and even "sparse" edge removals (where the sparse component is defined relative to the degree of the hypergraph), mirroring the role traditional expander graphs play. These robustness properties have significant implications in combinatorial optimization.

Research indicates that Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at zero-shot and few-shot natural language inference (NLI) when provided with examples, often surpassing specialized inferencing algorithms. This study investigates whether enabling LLMs to select appropriate NLI relations independently—without providing actual choices—yields superior results compared to offering multiple selection options (multiple-choice prompts). Through extensive evaluation across various architectures on three datasets (SNLI, CMNLI, and ROCStories), we establish that non-multiple-choice formulations generally produce higher performance scores than their multiple-choice counterparts. Furthermore, we observe a correlation: as output lengths increase in prompts featuring both examples and relational options, model accuracy tends to decline. Based on these findings, we conclude that utilizing direct generation rather than a multiple-choice framework is generally more effective for enhancing both computational efficiency and performance in LLM-based NLI tasks.

The low surface brightness (LSB) spiral UGC 8839 exhibits a rare trait: extreme off-axis star formation. This research utilizes new high-resolution optical and near-infrared imaging alongside [3.6]-[4.5]$\mu$m near-infrared color mapping of the galaxy's disk to investigate the spatial distribution of its stars. The findings reveal an annular ring of star formation situated between galactic radii of 3–12 $kpc$, with surface brightness peaking near 8–10 $kpc$. The MAVEN/NGIMS instrument detects gravity waves (GWs) within Mars' upper atmosphere through molecular density fluctuations, revealing signatures indicative of active GW propagation down to approximately 110 km altitude. As GW amplitude directly reflects the intensity of waves encountered, we analyzed correlations between GW signal strength and local climate factors—including latitude, season, solar cycle phase, and local time—using maximum likelihood regression fitted to our dataset. Our findings indicate latitude and seasonal variations significantly explain roughly 25% of the observed signal strength variability, with latitude exhibiting a stronger influence than seasonal shifts. GW signals strengthen near the polar regions across both hemispheres, displaying a distinct "double-dip" pattern during summer while remaining relatively uniform in the autumn and spring, with a pronounced minimum during the equatorial belt. Additionally, significant seasonal effects emerge around the latitudinal zones between 60° and 80°. No substantial correlation exists between GW signal strength and the solar cycle. In the southern hemisphere, the signal peaks at local morning and afternoon hours but diminishes throughout the day; conversely, in the northern hemisphere, day-night symmetry dominates except between 60° and 70° latitude where a clear morning maximum is evident.

This document outlines the latest advancements in Ultra-Peripheral Collisions, incidents characterized by the exchange of at least one virtual photon instead of nucleons during interactions. It examines theoretical concepts alongside experimental findings from LEP, as well as data obtained at SPS, TRISTAN, Tevatron, LHC, and the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider.

Although recent large-scale language models demonstrate impressive capabilities in reasoning and natural language comprehension, their applications in audio generation remain largely underdeveloped. This paper introduces an audio foundation model, AudioLLM-1, designed to transfer capabilities directly from large language models to the domain of audio generation. By training on a massive corpus comprising 1.8 trillion tokens of diverse raw waveforms, transcriptions, and labels, the model learns to autonomously generate not only high-quality audio but also corresponding text descriptions. Our comprehensive evaluation reveals that an in-depth, human-style prompt describing 10 to 20 attributes can guide the system to synthesize sounds that match user expectations, even challenging tasks like creating complex environmental sounds or extended musical pieces.

Recurrent Networks are extensively employed for sequential tasks, including Natural Language Processing and speech recognition, yet they are susceptible to training instability caused by exploding gradients. These issues have been largely mitigated by long-term dependency learning, a significant advancement in Recurrent Networks. This paper presents a new gating architecture, the Deep Bidirectional Gated Network (DBN), designed to reduce training difficulty and enhance the accuracy of Recurrent Bidirectional networks for language modeling. The model addresses specific limitations of prior designs, including Graded networks and Deep Bidirectional networks. Additionally, our approach allows for mini-batch training without necessitating a compromise compared to existing methods in terms of performance gains for sequential data. Deep Bidirectional networks demonstrate superior performance over other recurrent methods using the VOTe dataset for language modeling.

This study develops an economic model of pandemic propagation utilizing a standard SIR epidemiological framework, where each state transition represents "economic irreversibility"—the permanent reduction in economic activity caused by infection. By analyzing how quarantine measures and social distancing influence economic activity, infection dynamics, and policy timing, the authors establish criteria for selecting the optimal policy schedule. This schedule optimizes an objective function that balances economic welfare against policy costs. Furthermore, an sensitivity analysis is provided to quantify the trade-off between maximizing economic activity and minimizing the pandemic's spread.

Building on prior research that views machine learning model training as a cooperative game where data points are players, this paper introduces a new perspective by integrating the concept of transfer learning. We present a P-time algorithm to compute Shapley values exactly, addressing both regression and classification scenarios without relying on any specific assumptions regarding the loss function or feature distributions. We view Shapley values as the ideal solution for fairness and view them through a transfer learning lens, where data from one population train a model that is then deployed on another. Specifically, our proposed algorithm predicts the parameters of a classifier trained on future, unidentified players based on current observations. We validate the approach using extensive numerical experiments on real-world datasets, demonstrating its efficiency and high accuracy.

This study centers on discrete invariants that closely resemble Ltorentzn polynomials, with the primary conceptual link across these disciplines being invariant properties under Lorentzian transformation.

This work introduces an extensive experimental investigation into the magnetic ground states and transport properties of three triangular antiferromagnetic systems: Mn$_3$Sn, Mn$_3$Ge, and Mn$_3$Al. Our measurements identify that all three materials exhibit anomalous Hall effects arising from the non-collinear antiferromagnetic ordering within their structures. Furthermore, we observed that applying pressure significantly modulates the magnitude of the anomalous Hall effect in all samples. To provide a theoretical basis for these observations, we conducted first-principles calculations, which elucidated the mechanisms driving both the emergence of the non-collinear magnetic ground states and the pressure-induced variations in AHE strength. The study offers significant insights into the fundamental physics of magnetism and electronic transport in these materials, with broad implications for the development of future spintronics technologies based on non-collinear magnetic ordering.

A significant milestone in information technology is moving from unstructured to structured data formats. Relation Extraction (RE) plays a critical role in converting unstructured text within the structured data domain by identifying relations between entities. While Deep Learning (DL) methods have largely replaced traditional approaches for RE due to their superior performance, these Deep Learning models often fail at zero-shot settings because they require numerous labeled examples to learn features effectively. To address this limitation, this paper introduces a novel unsupervised feature representation approach utilizing Self-supervised Learning (SLSL) to identify features without relying on labeled data. Our method consists of two components: (1) Tokenization based on character-level patterns and (2) Relation Matching derived from pre-trained language models. Extensive experiments conducted across three datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing baselines in both few-shot and zero-shot RE scenarios. Furthermore, this method is model-light and computationally efficient.

Graphs serve as fundamental tools for analyzing complex systems, yet recent progress relies increasingly on generalizing to higher-order structures through objects like hypergraphs, which capture multi-way relationships. The mathematical properties of such higher-order networks have garnered significant attention in physics and mathematical biology. Specifically, understanding phase transitions within random higher-order graphs is essential for modeling abrupt shifts in large-scale biological and ecological dynamics. This paper introduces a novel approach to generating an ensemble of stochastic hypergraphs, akin to an exponential random graph model. By applying a higher-order variant of the configuration method, we derive a corresponding in-degree and out-degree-based multi-way mobility model. Furthermore, we investigate these networks using techniques from statistical mechanics, linking their global graph theoretic attributes to the underlying stochastic generation process. Finally, we highlight potential applications of this framework in various physical and biological contexts.

Anatomical details are crucial for the interpretation and analysis of medical imaging datasets; however, this information is often unstructured and semi-structured. Integrating anatomical knowledge into the analysis of radiological and nuclear imaging data holds the potential to enhance diagnostic capabilities and therapeutic strategies. While numerous studies have explored how medical image features correlate with treatment outcomes, fewer have incorporated anatomical information. To address this gap, this paper introduces a comprehensive review of anatomical data within the context of radiation oncology and positron emission tomography (PET). We propose a data-centric framework for organizing and anatomical labeling that supports machine learning applications. The paper concludes by outlining current limitations and offering future directions for the effective utilization of anatomical information in PET and radiotherapy.

This study presents an approach to characterizing manifolds admitting taut foliations or tight contact structures with Euler classes $e(M)$ satisfying $|e(M)| \leq 3$. The method involves constructing candidate contact structures by surgically modifying existing contact structures that realize $e(M)$ via an integer, where our framework provides sufficient conditions for maintaining tightness. When applied to closed 3-manifolds obtained by connected sum of closed, irreducible 3-manifolds each possessing a known tight contact structure—specifically those with metric between two given values—the results yield significant findings. Notably, we demonstrate that three specific candidate contact structures were initially excluded; yet two subsequently prove tight, thereby establishing that three previously unproven 3-manifolds support taut foliations.

This work introduces a robust metric for characterizing unidirectional emission in microcavity lasers. While Shannon entropy applied to far-field distributions—calculated within polar coordinates to ascertain directional symmetry—offers a versatile and intuitive approach, it serves as an effective tool for assessing loss mechanisms governing unidirectionality microcavities suffer from. We demonstrate that high-precision predictions regarding the stability of photonases induced by parasitic scattering centers are achievable. Furthermore, this methodology enables precise tuning of such defects to control photonases in microcavities laser systems.

This paper conducts a risk-return analysis of cryptocurrencies alongside major financial assets to evaluate their viability as long-term store-of-value instruments. Risk is quantified using linear regressions, where standard deviations serve as residual errors, enabling comparison via standard mean-standard deviation frameworks. Results indicate that select cryptocurrencies exhibit mean returns comparable to major assets but suffer from significantly higher volatility. Consequently, unless utility values are factored into investor decision-making, current investment strategies suggest these digital currencies are unsuitable for use as long-term stores of wealth.

We address the large deviations in one-dimensional instances of the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) equation during its short-time evolution by employing a technique known as the path integral saddle point approach. This method yields to the one-dimensional KPZ model's exact results across its short-time evolutionary phases in its large deviations. Our findings align perfectly with previous calculations based on stochastic test-function techniques, thereby validating their applicability to the KPZ model's one-dimensional evolutionary phases. Additionally, we examine various asymptotic regimes, specifically focusing on transitions between regimes as features like quadratic term dominance shift, and observe how results behave when considering dimensionless parameters like surface tension variations, and we investigate how these changes in parameters affect the underlying stochastic processes' characteristics.

Compressive plasma turbulence occurring within the solar wind is investigated using data from the Parker Solar Probe. We apply Bayesian model comparison to evaluate four distinct theoretical frameworks—compressible inertial Alfvén wave (CIT), compressible inertial Alfvén wave with parallel gradients (CIP), ion acoustic (IAW), and magnetosonic (MSW)—against in-situ measurements. These theoretical predictions were tested against compressive velocity spectra derived from the spacecraft velocity variance, specifically utilizing the cross-product of velocity components perpendicular to the mean magnetic field. Furthermore, velocity phase shifts were utilized to determine the direction of wave propagation parallel to the magnetic field. Our analysis indicates that observed spectral morphologies and propagation directions are most consistent with either IAW or MSW. A notable finding is that these predictions hold true across a broad range of Alfvénic fluctuations, demonstrating that the characteristics remain largely independent of Alfvénicity levels.

This study introduces a technique to characterize and refine the pulse duration and coherence characteristics of X-ray Free Electron Lasers (FELs) utilizing a single crystal silicon sample. This approach offers a viable solution for future facilities generating coherent soft X-rays with pulse durations reaching femtosecond-level coherence, a regime where typical FEL pulse coherence times usually span from several to hundreds of femtoseconds. We have developed a theoretical framework grounded in hard X-ray diffraction analysis to elucidate observed diffraction patterns arising from an interaction between pulse duration and coherence time. Our calculations demonstrate that when diffraction patterns are averaged across many pulses, information regarding the pulse's coherence time can be retrieved, enabling direct experimental measurement within the specified parameters.

This work investigates a mathematical model for buoyancy-driven flows that integrate thermal conduction effects and allow for vertical temperature gradients. The physical context is described by the full Navier-Stokes and the energy equations alongside a specific equation of state, within a framework allowing for both integral and differential forms for the state relationship and allowing for both weak and specific forms. To facilitate this, we employ the Boussinesq approximation in a generalized manner and assume a specific type of weak form for the state relationship that includes the possibility of a vertical temperature gradient. By utilizing this model, we demonstrate the existence of a mathematical equilibrium where flow and temperature distributions satisfy our assumptions. Additionally, we extend our previous work to consider a more complex state relationship that includes both thermal expansion and possible non-ideal effects. By extending the model to include both weak forms for both types of state relationships, we demonstrate that mathematical equilibrium always exists in both cases.

Gerrymandering represents a distortion of elections achieved through the manipulation of voting district boundaries, enabling one political faction to secure an unfair majority despite lacking broad popular support. This phenomenon persists globally today, causing significant concern within the United States amidst growing pressure for legislative remedies. While numerous research groups have attempted to identify districting algorithms that prevent such electoral fraud, these efforts often fail because the problems they address are computationally intractable. Our study offers a fresh methodology to overcome these inherent limitations by reimagining districting through the lens of flow network optimization. This approach offers a balanced compromise between structural fairness and political efficacy. Through computational modeling, we propose, design, and refine algorithms that generate districting plans incorporating these innovative features. Our results demonstrate that plan produced by our methods yield superior outcomes when evaluated against established metrics of governance, political efficiency, and equity.

This study introduces an objective line-cytic system designed to detect defects in patterned fabric using the GHOG descriptor for image representation. The proposed method relies on phase correlation to align defective fabric images with ideal samples, followed by vector subtraction between the reference and target images to identify anomalies. To validate our approach, we conducted experiments utilizing the GAIT-1 dataset, comparing performance metrics including those from the traditional ISFI competition. The results demonstrate that the proposed technique achieves a high accuracy of 93.41%.

We investigate the rate of change of the Bondi mass within Einstein's gravitational framework. Theory dictates that the Bondi mass rate of change must adhere to an upper bound of $c^4/G$, a limit notably aligned with Dyson's concept of maximum luminosity. We demonstrate that this constraint arises simply because the rate of change is restricted by the eigenvalues of the Weyl tensor, specifically its "Weyl spin." Consequently, the radiation's Weyl characteristics—such as those defining multipole moments—govern the strength of this limit. When the emitted radiation lacks significant Weyl contributions, the bound approximates Dyson's original derivation. Furthermore, we propose using the derived expression to set an upper bound on the rate of change of a black hole's horizon area.

Population III (III) star binary remnants are anticipated to form in the earliest galaxies and accumulate within nuclear regions as compact clusters due to dynamical interactions. Consequently, these systems are expected to merge at redshift $z > 0$ within galactic nuclei, potentially producing gravitational waves detectable by next-generation detectors. This work examines Pop III binary coalescences occurring within the first decade of a galaxy's life, specifically at $0 \leq z \leq 10$, focusing on binary black holes (BBHs) and neutron star pairs (NS-NS). We present a methodology to estimate the number of binary coalescences occurring at high redshifts ($z > 0$) within galactic nuclei, factoring in the initial binary population size, cluster demographics, and relevant astrophysical parameters. Utilizing a representative sample of 1,000 simulations, we infer that Pop III binaries constitute a substantial source for future gravitational wave detections. In grid systems featuring energy storage units (ESS), conventional frequency-based observation methods struggle to identify location-specific supply-demand imbalances, which hinders their effectiveness. Conventional approaches often mandate continuous, high-frequency status checks of ESS, resulting in substantial communication costs. To mitigate this, we introduce a Decentralized Learning-based Storage-centric Load Balancing (DLSS-LB) scheme designed to autonomously determine the most appropriate time for ESS charge or discharge operations. The DLSS-LB framework consists of two core mechanisms: (i) a decentralized learning process where each ESS system acquires its own load and load-derivative data using localized models, thereby estimating load conditions within its immediate vicinity; and (ii) a performance-driven decision engine that leverages the load and its derivative information to balance overall system performance against monitoring expenses. Extensive testing across a realistic microgrid environment demonstrates that DLSS-LB successfully reduces communication expenses by approximately 50% compared to existing solutions.

Text-based games provide an excellent framework for evaluating language comprehension, complex problem-solving, and common-sense inference in virtual agents, yet their performance remains constrained by legacy tooling, allowing only about 300 steps per second. We introduce TextWorldExpress, a high-performance version supporting three prominent game benchmarks that improves processing speed by a factor of 1,000, exceeding one million simulation steps per second off-the-shelf hardware. This dramatic boost cuts down computation times, allowing researchers to conduct experiments involving a billion states within roughly a day.

We examine transport in edges formed by edge dislocations situated on Topological Insulators (TIs), where edges dislocations act as "line defects" that carve out topologically non-contractible regions consisting of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ monopoles of spin connections. Consequently, these regions host unique modes of edge spin textures characteristic of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ monopoles, giving rise to spin-dependent quantum interference in a transport context. Our analysis demonstrates that when two such defects intersect, they produce characteristic signatures of transport that can be used to uniquely identify $\mathbb{Z}_2$ TI surface states through edge spin textures associated with these line defects. These findings suggest new experimental avenues for investigating topologically protected phenomena within $\mathbb{Z}_2$ TIs utilizing mesoscopic transport techniques.

This study investigates the joint extreme probabilities and spatial correlations among wind speed and significant wave height within the North East Atlantic, specifically from the Faroe Islands to the coast of North America. Utilizing data from over 100 buoys spanning the period 2010–2014, we demonstrate that spatial extremal dependence in both variables is significantly stronger than what is predicted by standard Gaussian correlation models, with the upper tail of significant wave height exhibiting a slightly higher dependence than wind speed tails. Furthermore, we apply a bivariate Generalized Extreme Value model to a subset of buoy datasets to estimate local extremal dependence. Our findings indicate that, on average, the estimated parameters show consistency, although significant spatial heterogeneity exists. Consequently, we propose adapting the standard Generalized Extreme Value analysis framework to better capture these extremal behaviors.

By utilizing ellipsoids to model sequential potential movements, the algorithm can resolve inherent ambiguities found in trajectory acquisition data. Consequently, the resulting learned behavior exhibits higher quality without requiring any form of manual adjustment or post-processing treatment by researchers.

We introduce an novel approach for single-view 3D object pose estimation that leverages three-dimensional objects detected in outdoor, in-real-life video streams. These videos serve as valuable data sources because they feature diverse viewpoints, natural background illumination, varied camera settings, numerous poses, and varied environmental conditions. We further establish a new benchmark dataset comprising 3D-bounded boxes across more than 600 hours of in-real-life video footage captured from single-camera setups. Remarkably, our method achieves superior performance for single-view 3D pose estimation on standard benchmarks, utilizing only previously published data on 3D-bounded boxes for training, without access to additional training-specific information. Source code and model weights are available at https://github.com/zhangyongzheng/inwild-3d-obj-pose.

Despite ongoing efforts to combat misinformation surrounding COVID-19 vaccines, many people remain undecided in favor of vaccination. This study investigates how such misinformation influences individuals' decisions to reject or accept vaccines by examining two concepts: Susceptibility (the tendency to believe false information) and Resilience (the capacity to withstand the impact of the information). By analyzing data from 105 participants in the U.S. who evaluated misinformation content related to vaccines during fall 2021, the research found a strong association between these psychosocial factors and vaccination intent. Specifically, susceptibility played a more significant role in determining rejection than resilience did, yet both were more influential than the misconception's objective accuracy. These findings underscore the critical need to address misinformation through targeted interventions designed to bolster immunity while reducing susceptibility.

Attosecond physics has seen rapid growth over the last fifteen years, driven by breakthroughs in high-order harmonic generation and the creation of linearly polarized, broadband attosecond pulses. However, progress is hindered by limitations in conversion efficiency and temporal resolution. To foster future advancements in attosecond science, it is crucial to achieve two key objectives: raising efficiency in harmonic emission and shortening the attosecond pulse duration. Here, we introduce a strategy that employs multi-wave mixing within a white-light continuum to boost harmonic yield. Furthermore, the use of optical chirp in a broadband continuum allows for the generation of very short attosecond bursts. Collectively, these contributions demonstrate the value of combining distinct plasma harmonic generation pathways with the techniques already established for attosecond pulse formation.

Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have demonstrated significant potential in solving physics-governed partial differential equations (PDEs), especially in scenarios with scarce data. Although existing generalizable approaches rely on a learnable time-scaling scalar to handle variable PDEs temporally, these methods often yield suboptimal outcomes when applied to systems featuring complex temporal trends. Furthermore, we enhance algorithmic stability by integrating a revised runge-kutta method into the loss calculation to mitigate steep error surfaces, and by scaling the loss components to mitigate numerical imbalances. The proposed methodology was validated across three representative PDE scattering scenarios. Comparative analyses against established generalized solutions underscore the superior accuracy of our new scalar mechanism.

Understanding the surface composition of terrestrial exoplanets is crucial for characterizing their formation and subsequent evolution, yet their bulk composition remains largely constrained by the stellar parameters and planetary orbits. This design successfully maintains the required potential flatness, yields a Starobinsky model featuring an $\xi R^2$ term in the effective gravity, and generatesStochastic gravitational waves with amplitudes governed by specific numerical coefficients.

Nonreciprocal optical systems are essential for photonic technologies, offering ways to break time-reversal symmetry to control light propagation, such as through direction-dependent differences in how photon pairs correlate and how they physically travel. While previous research has linked nonreciprocal effects with entangled photon pair nonreciprocity—specifically, directional disparities in their quantum statistical properties—we observed a similar phenomenon using photons generated by quantum-well slabs within a coupled ring-resononcer structure. Our experiments demonstrate a direction-specific difference in the probability of detecting doublets of photons, implying a new, previously unexplored form of breaking time-reversal symmetry involving quantum statistics rather than just phase or transport properties. This effect provides a potential new method for detecting or measuring nonreciprocal optical properties based on the unique behavior of particle-pair quantum statistics across directions in these systems.

Superconducting quantum circuits have emerged as a leading platform in quantum technology, enabling rapid scaling of multi-qubit processors. Their progress has been constrained by material defects, necessitating a deeper understanding of lossy elements at the single-qubit level to ensure continued growth. We introduce a framework for characterizing interfacial imperfections between superconducting qubits and the microwave resonator used for readout and control. By simultaneously fitting theoretical models to experimental pulse-response data, we quantify the effective resistance and energy dissipation of the coupling capacitor within the readout chain, accounting for total capacitance as well as the resistance and reactance of the interface. We validate this approach by applying it to both high-coherence and lower-performing qubits, illustrating how these properties dictate stored state lifetime and measurement fidelity. Ultimately, we demonstrate that refined fabrication can suppress coupling-layer resistance sufficiently to isolate qubit decoherence sources outside the system, an essential requirement for future quantum architectures.

This paper examines infinite matrix theory through the lens of Hausdorff's research on partitions of $\mathbb{R}$ into Borel sets and his definition of a class $\mathcal{H}$ comprising bounded Hausdorff matrices. By utilizing standard sufficient matrix invariants such as the Permutationally Positive cone and Monotone Convergence methods, along with our derived necessary conditions for class membership, we establish that the subset of $\mathcal{H}$ satisfying these criteria is dense and otherwise fully characterizes such matrices through this approach.

Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs) represent the single most enduring and lucrative strategy for investors, yet the specific trading signals responsible for their success remain a subject of debate. This study addresses a critical flaw in prior research: the potential selection bias inherent in traditionally isolating individual trading signals. By modeling CTAs as a blended approach to multiple strategies, we demonstrate that classic strategies—specifically trend following, mean reversion, and risk management—are compromised by the presence of short-term reversal traders. Consequently, only signals engineered to remain robust despite short-term traders can succeed, which is precisely what enables long-term investment success in this sector.

Protocol detection involves the critical task of identifying protocols at the application layer, which is essential for maintaining overall network security. The primary challenge lies in distinguishing protocols accurately, particularly when the relevant data is heavily corrupted by noise. *Dedecide* is a passive protocol detection framework designed to address these limitations through the novel concept of "protocol decide trees." This approach enables efficient and precise protocol detection even when dealing with extremely noisy data, leveraging a new feature called "protocol signature." By capturing the characteristic behavior of protocols within the input-output relationships of consecutive transactions, this signature distinguishes our method from existing solutions that typically analyze only traffic patterns or content details. Experimental evaluations demonstrate significant improvements in both precision and speed, highlighting the utility and effectiveness of the dedecide system.

This paper introduces a novel all-electronic spin-wave transducer, designed to convert microwave signals into magnons. Introduced as a promising information carrier in magnetoelectric systems, magnonics holds significant potential for future computing applications. Our proposed structure consists of a thin yttrium iron yttrium orthorochondro ($YIG$) layer coupled capacitively to an interdigital microwave idumuctor. By employing a finite element method within frequency domain simulations, we demonstrate that this configuration resonates within a specific bandwidth, effectively exciting magnons at that resonance. Furthermore, to investigate the transducer's performance from a circuit analysis standpoint, we develop an equivalent circuit model capable of accurately reflecting experimental observations and facilitating the exploration of various designs.

Federated learning (FL) represents a distributed machine learning approach that ensures user privacy by restricting access to user data, making data sharing unnecessary during training. This work introduces a novel adaptive federated learning algorithm designed to accelerate regular FL operations by selectively incorporating data samples based on their label confidence. Comprehensive evaluations on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses standard FL benchmarks in performance and closely matches centralized learning outcomes, showcasing both efficient acceleration and near-optimal accuracy.

This Letter introduces a theoretical framework designed for comprehensive optical analysis of high-dimensional Greenberger-Horne-Zeinberger (GHZ) resources. The study initially validates this methodology through complete measurements of distinct three-photon GHZ states within a tripartite quantum basis. The approach is subsequently generalized, with a full photonic hyper-entanglement and quantum Fourier transform integration. The utility of this proposal extends towards enhanced multi-photon capabilities for both quantum computing and quantum communications in higher-order dimensions of entanglement.

This study investigates uplink channel estimation within intelligent-reflecting-surface (IRS)-assisted multi-user systems, where direct line-of-sight links between the base station (BS) and user equipment (UE) are absent, and communication occurs solely via a single-type reflection path. The primary objective is to minimize uplink pilot power while ensuring a designated accuracy threshold for channel estimation. To achieve this, we introduce an alternating optimization framework that separately updates power allocation for the UE and IRS phase alignment coefficients using the Maximum Likelihood estimation method derived from up-downlink channel reciprocity. By applying relaxed diagonal approximation to tensor-based problems and employing stochastic approximation for continuous optimization, efficient and near-optimal solutions are generated with low computational complexity. Simulation results confirm the proposed scheme outperforms existing benchmarks, delivering significant reductions in pilot power with minimal performance loss relative to standard methods.

We conducted an analysis of local news coverage during the pandemic using a dataset comprising over 1.5 million articles from 900 U.S. markets, which we contextualized with daily national statistics on cases, deaths, and hospitalization. Our findings revealed that while initial news interest spiked in correlation with death rates, this correlation weakened significantly as the pandemic progressed. Additionally, we identified distinct patterns in the timing and intensity of coverage across different media types—distinguishing between general local outlets and their respective opinion, news, and analysis sections—and examined how these varied based on the political leaning of each publication.

Counting represents a critical milestone in human cognitive development, a process whose acquisition remains poorly understood. Recent studies have demonstrated that both adults and toddlers exhibit a performance decline or "interference" when navigating between metric systems; specifically, the interference caused by training on ordinal language can disrupt the acquisition of cardinal systems. A recent theoretical framework explains this by proposing "cardinal learning" and "ordinal learning" as distinct systems that compete for representation within the brain's number line. A recent study provides new data supporting this "two-systems" theory by revealing a developmental milestone around age 4. Before this point, children generally possess only one dominant system, whereas after it has emerged, they typically develop two separate systems that overlap and occasionally conflict. This inflection stage is not merely a transition phase but rather represents a period of increased plasticity in which children's brains reorganize to support full cardinal learning alongside existing ordinal knowledge. Understanding this mechanism is crucial for developing more effective educational strategies and interventions for individuals who struggle with numerical proficiency.

Bloom filters are extensively employed to approximate set membership and operate with a controlled, bounded error rate. Building on this, Sun et al. introduced the concept of the cuckoo filter, which substitutes Bloom filters by utilizing polynomial hash functions. This new approach surpasses existing ones by supporting the deletion of individual entries, maintaining a constant error rate regardless of load, and enabling the discovery of any false positive configuration with bounded time. This study presents a theoretical analysis of cuckoo filters, establishing the theoretical underpinnings previously proposed by Sun et al. Specifically, we utilize percolation theory to derive a user-friendly formula for calculating the false positive rate, a result that aligns with both theoretical predictions and practical observations. Furthermore, we examine the runtime complexity of generating and generating exact estimates of the filter's false positive rate, demonstrating supercomputer-level parallel processing capabilities that can be harnessed for distributed caching systems. This research provides a user-friendly formula for calculating the filter's error rate, aligning theoretical predictions with practical observations. This result paves the way for advanced applications in distributed caching systems.

This paper explores multiple connections between convex geometry and the theory of holomorphic functions on complex planes. As a primary finding, an analog of Brunn-Minkowski theory is developed for positive products, establishing analogs of key results concerning mixed volumes and the Minkowski inequality. Furthermore, an analog of the Aleksandrov-Fenchel inequalities is proven for the positive product of pluriharmonic functions. These findings yield multiple applications. For instance, new instances of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality are derived for the pointwise product of superharmonic functions defined on convex subsets of Euclidean space, while it is demonstrated that the volume of the complex projection of a convex body onto complex planes adheres to a specific Brunn-Minkowski-type inequality.

This study introduces a market microstructure model where future prices depend on the trading volume within each unit of time, utilizing the standard agent-based framework. We propose an extended agent-based paradigm in which prices evolve functionally of time-based volume metrics rather than aggregate values alone. We propose a new agent-based framework where future prices depend on the time-honored model of dependency on total volume traded within each unit of time. We propose an extension of the agent-based framework where future prices depend on the time-honored model of dependency on total volume traded within each unit of time.

This study introduces FLDA (Federated Learning Decentralized Anonymity), a privacy-preserving method capable of robustly withstanding Byzantine attacks in federated learning environments. By employing a consensus-driven communication protocol and a secure stochastic masking protocol, FLDA ensures the confidentiality of user data during the learning process. We have proven mathematically that FLDA converges to $(\mathcal G, \mathcal f)$-smooth functions and remains secure, ensuring privacy despite the presence of an omniscient malicious attacker. Our experimental results demonstrate that FLDA outperforms both existing defense mechanisms and baseline systems, exhibiting superior robustness and accuracy while maintaining user privacy.

We propose a novel algorithm for autonomous driving that employs machine learning to train an agent capable of learning to handle traffic scenarios by interacting with a simulated driving environment. The system's objective is to minimize the long-term average cost, defined as the average of instantaneous costs incurred over time, where an instantaneous cost represents the proportion of time the autonomous vehicle (AV) occupies any of the following states: fully blocked by a human-driven vehicle (HDV), partially obstructed within the lane of a HDV, near intersections or road edges, or moving at excessive speed. By simulating interactions between the AV and HDs, the method effectively captures the Markov Decision Process required for solving the average-cost MDP, leveraging both simulated data and real-world data to train the policy. When tested on a dataset comprising 21 hours of footage from the NCSU data collection, this approach demonstrated superior performance compared to leading baselines assessed under identical conditions.

While there is growing interest in creating defenses against such forgeries, attention to the ethical ramifications of emerging technologies remains scarce. In this work, we offer a comprehensive overview of current approaches for identifying deepfakes, covering various architectures and proposed solutions. We then assess the limitations of these methods and propose strategies for further investigation. The identification and subsequent characterization of sub-Neptune-sized exoplanets have intensified community inquiries into the habitability conditions of such worlds, particularly focusing on the feasibility of liquid water oceans given their often dense atmospheres. While prior research addressed the atmospheric thermodynamics, our work evaluates how the composition of the deep interior influences the planetary envelope and surface temperature, specifically targeting oceanic habitability. We modeled the thermal profiles of several potentially rocky sub-Neptudes situated in the habitable zone, utilizing a diffusion equation for atmospheric composition and a power-law model for the interior. Specifically, we assessed the effects found in sub-Neptudes similar to TOI-133b, TOI-1426c, and TOI-312d, discovering that even if the core possesses substantial water, a liquid surface water layer cannot exist unless these planets have lost significant mass.

This paper investigates the capacity of two-layer spiking neuronal networks to acquire sequential actions. We demonstrate that these networks can effectively learn temporal patterns and sequence predictions even when synaptic connections are binary and the underlying weight distribution is symmetric. However, we find that performance is markedly improved when network connectivity is asymmetric, finding support in both empirical data and theoretical analysis. Furthermore, we show that Bienenstock-Cooper-Munro plasticity rules, which lack explicit normalization, suffice for sequence prediction within this framework. These findings contribute to our understanding of how simple biological mechanisms enable robust sequence learning in the brain.

This paper introduces a novel training paradigm for Optical Character Recognition (OCR) based on Self-Training under Supervision-less conditions, which reimagines the strategies for constructing public text datasets. Although contemporary OCR algorithms have attained remarkable performance on benchmarks like Total-Text, they remain vulnerable to unseen text instances never encountered during training, largely due to over-reliance on annotated data and the prohibitive cost of creating additional annotations. To counter this, we propose SSL-ST, enhancing OCR capabilities by mitigating data dependency through several core modules tailored for semi-supervisory learning without using it extensively. Specifically, our approach incorporates Semi-supervisory mask training, Semi-supervisory consistency training, and Semi-supervisory pseudo-labeling to bolster text instance detection and recognition while leveraging the inherent characteristics of public text datasets. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed methods. Furthermore, our experiments reveal that this new framework yields superior performance gains compared to state-of-the-art solutions.

This study investigates how generalized polynomial chaos (gPC) expansion serves as an efficient technique for solving differential equations that feature stochastic coefficients. Under specific smoothness conditions, we analyze the spectral convergence properties of this method. Furthermore, drawing upon the spectral convergence of gPC as a foundation, we introduce and evaluate a novel approach for deriving posterior confidence intervals in inverse problems.

In industrial settings, managing high-dimensional data presents a significant obstacle to creating efficient, real-time monitoring methods. To address this, monitoring techniques must be paired with dimensionality reduction strategies. While many such approaches exist, our goal in this paper is to introduce a unified framework that simplifies and expands potential solutions. This framework outlines the steps out of the box, making it easy to adapt or extend existing methods while enhancing performance. To validate this concept, we applied the framework to both a synthetic dataset and a real-world case: the continuous casting process in a steel plant.

We evaluate whether recent discoveries of accreted dwarf galaxies and the Gaia-Sausage Enceladus (GSE) structure align with the classic, highly dissipative merger paradigm that formed the Galaxy. Our analysis indicates that both the LMS-1 (Wukong) dwarf and Hydra A exhibit low intrinsic dissipativity, as does the GSE. Although the GSE displays a substantial radial anisotropy, its radial extent suggests it did not originate from a major merger event. Instead, we propose that Milky Way assembly resulted from numerous accretions involving numerous small satellites rather than a handful of massive dwarf galaxies. This numerous-dwarfs-scenario is further corroborated by simulations targeting random encounters with numerous dwarf dwarfs, which successfully reproduce the broad structural and chemical heterogeneity observed today. This approach also clarifies why both the GSE and recent discoveries like LMS-1 and Wukong show similar chemical abundances despite differing kinematics and radial orbits.

For a profinite group $G$ and a topological abelian group $M$ (where the topology on $M$ is discrete), we develop a continuous homological theory profinite group cohomology for the pair $(GM)$. This leads us to examine this profinite group cohomology via a $SGM$-homotopy spectral sequence. This investigation yields two main results: first, a specific case where a certain homotopy profinite group $SGM$-homological spectral sequence occurs; second, an isomorphism that establishes the isomorphism of the continuous homological profinite group $M$-to $MG$-homology. These two findings are demonstrated with the help of a certain finiteness assumption. This implies that the continuous homology of a profinite group $GM$ can be utilized to derive a certain homotopy profinite group $SGM$-homology.

We introduce SAEA-Invoice, a comprehensive multi-level dataset constructed from real-world invoices. Although existing extraction models perform well on invoices—often regarded as the archetype of document digitization—they typically falter when confronted with more document varieties, each bearing distinct visual structures. This phenomenon arises because extracting information constitutes a specific instance of a broader visual task adapted to document types; consequently, training individual models for every structure wastes both development resources and, most critically, valuable annotated data. To address this inefficiency, we propose a novel approach, SAE-AE, which synthesizes documents via a specific architecture into an abstract representation space before adapting it to different document structures. Specifically, we employ SAAE as a robust document encoder to reduce dimensionality and extract abstract characteristics, then adapt these learned features using a transformer-based encoder for document type classification and extraction tasks, thereby enabling SAE-AE to generalize across invoices, receipts, and more complex documents like bills and statements. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on invoices and substantially surpasses current benchmarks on complex receipt and statement datasets.

The European sulfur (EuS) monolayer positioned on an antimonene-substitited InAs buffer layer—a specific interface bondingscheme offers promising applications for spintronics. This particular configuration results in a EuS valence band maximum situated 0.13 eV below that of InS, facilitating a robust van der Waals interaction characterized by significant charge transfer. This interaction not only preserves the intrinsic honeycomb lattice structure of standalone EuS monolayers but also transforms the electronic landscape, lifting the traditional spin-splitting observed in free-standing EuS monolayers to 0 eV. Across various bonding arrangements, we observe that the EuS valence band maximum consistently falls 0 to 0.13 eV beneath that of InS, ensuring strong van der Waals coupling in all cases. While these configurations induce charge transfer that deforms the band structure, they maintain the fundamental EuS honeycomb lattice integrity. Notably, specific bondingscenarios exhibit type-II band structures featuring maximums and minimums separated vertically, suggesting potential for in-plane spin polarization of thermoelectric currents.

Training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) necessitates vast quantities of annotated images, a challenging and costly endeavor. Furthermore, introducing a newly labeled dataset often results in performance degradation when combining it with existing ones in transfer learning due to distribution shifts between training and testing data. Distribution alignment techniques using public data can mitigate this but suffer from increased domain distance and introduced noise; additionally, they impose significant computational costs during both source and target data processing. Addressing these limitations, this paper introduces ClickTrain, a framework designed to enhance both the accuracy and efficiency of such training processes without relying on external augmentation. By leveraging an automated, domain-agnostic object detection model, ClickTrain enables effective use of unannotated data alongside existing sets while circumventing the pitfalls associated with standard transfer learning approaches. Experiments conducted across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that ClickTrain achieves performance on par with, and in certain cases superior to existing methods, using only target data without any auxiliary support.

This research explores extensions to bounded distributive residuated lattices and distributes over their join operations. We introduce diverse types of representational extensions, examining conservativity, completeness, and canonical morphisms associated with them, alongside distribution patterns for diverse forms of extensions in these residuous structures.

The LIGO–Virco collaboration has reported three gravitational-wave signals originating from compact binary mergers involving black holes and neutron stars. Identifying these sources is vital for assessing future detection prospects and refining population constraints on these objects. Although the first two signals stemmed from black hole–black hole mergers, the third involved neutron stars within a binary system. Although such binary neutron star detections are increasingly probable with extended observation, binary neutron star mergers also emit electromagnetic (EM) radiation in contrast to black hole mergers. Detecting this concurrent EM output would allow scientists to pinpoint the binary neutron star merger site and investigate the physics of neutron star matter through multi-messenger astronomy.

This study investigates the connection between host star metallicity and the characteristics of giant planets through the compilation of 206 confirmed discoveries from the planet hunter organization. Using empirical metallicity estimates (derived via EMP), we correlated these values with the metallicities of the corresponding stars. For the majority of cases, the majority of these findings align well with contemporary expectations that higher metallicity in host stars correlates with a greater likelihood of possessing giant planets.

This paper addresses a class of control problems designated as constrained Markov decision process (CMDP), which aims to maximize an optimal policy's performance on a specific criterion while ensuring adherence to a limit on their associated cost constraint. Within the context of single-item inventory control, which features both fixed ordering costs and backorders, the work establishes that the dual formulation provides an effective approximation for the minimum achievable conditional risk exposure measure at a given confidence level. Notably, this approximation holds regardless of whether an ordering policy follows an $(s, S)$ structure or a more general variation. The research further establishes the $1$-approximation bound for the problem, demonstrating that computational effort can remain low if the underlying stochastic demand distribution supports a particular property. Finally, numerical investigations are conducted to evaluate proposed theoretical results alongside the efficacy of an iterative heuristic designed to derive near-optimal policies.

This study introduces a novel approach for automatically transcribing handwritten mathematical notation by utilizing an extended Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture designed to perform multi-class segmentation of specific symbols. While segmentation serves as a fundamental step in recognizing mathematical scripts, existing solutions struggle with defining appropriate scanner functions and selecting optimal parameters. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing a two-stage pipeline: first, a rough segmentation via a primary CNN, followed by a secondary, localized refinement process using another CNN. This method demonstrates promising preliminary results in transcribing a handwritten form of LaTeX.

We employ the localization technique on the resolved conifold to analyze supersymmetric quantum mechanics confined to a Lagrangian 3-cycle. Our findings demonstrate that in the BPS phase, the state count corresponds precisely to the twisted Dolbeault cohomology classes of the resolved space, whereas non-BPS phases yield both quantum corrections and contributions from the conifold's boundary cycle. Notably, these results can be replicated through an application of the matrix model approach described in arXiv:1409.2389.

Research into how viral outbreaks spread through social contacts has heavily favored homogeneous network structures due to their analytical simplicity, even though these networks are less representative of real-world scenarios. In contrast, there is a growing focus on how varied and heterogeneous network architectures influence the dynamics of infectious diseases. This study introduces a stochastic network model characterized by distinct node types, wherein each type possesses unique parameters

Actor-critic methods constitute the cornerstone of reinforcement learning yet face the critical challenge of policy optimization, which is plagued by high variance in standard approaches. While recent strategies attempt to mitigate this issue, a more fundamental solution lies in Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), which offers superior performance over standard Markov Chain Monte Carlo techniques. By incorporating HMC, we construct an efficient policy that balances exploration and exploitation effectively. Specifically, we introduce the Critic-HMC module, which leverages the HMC optimizer to refine the policy, thereby reducing optimization variance and enhancing sample efficiency. Experimental results indicate that actor-critic algorithms equipped with the Critic-HMC module surpass conventional actor-critic methods in sample efficiency and achieve performance comparable to, or exceeding, more complex algorithms within various control tasks.

It is established that every prime number $p \geq 5$ can be expressed in the form $6k \pm 1$ for some integer $k$. Although necessary for this property, this representation is not sufficient, as numbers of this form are not guaranteed to be prime. This study aims to identify specific values of $k$ for which $6k \pm 1$ is composite. We define two sequences of integers derived from Fibonacci numbers: $A_n = F_{2n+1} - 1$ and $B_n = F_{2n+1} + 1$. Consequently, numbers within these sets offer significant for generating $6k \pm 1$ composites. Specifically, elements of type $6k_ {A_n}$ always yield a Fibonacci number of form prime, as do those of form $6k_ {B_n}$. We demonstrate that for all n, the Fibonacci number $6k_ {A_n}$ is divisible by 10, as are most forms related Fibonacci number, as do form divisible 35.

This paper presents a new probabilistic SLA framework called PSC, designed for autonomous navigation in dynamic settings where sensor data is inconsistent. Since standard approaches rely on dependable sensor inputs, they often fail when environmental factors, such as adverse weather, degrade signal quality. To address this, the proposed method utilizes a probabilistic fusion process that manages variations in sensor reliability, including cases where a sensor provides no useful information, by defining a specific "unreliable sensor distribution" and integrating it into the algorithm. Validation through simulations based on a real-world robot navigation scenario demonstrates the method's efficacy in enhancing robustness, particularly when one or more sensors function poorly.

Nereid, Neptune's third-largest moon, exhibits a red spectral slope that contrasts sharply with those of other Neptunian moons. Through spectral analysis spanning 0.4 to 2.5 $\mu$m, we investigate the origins of this specific slope alongside the spectral features of other Triton-like objects—those displaying neutral slopes—potentially revealing a shared composition distinct from standard Neptunian moons like Nereid. Using a comprehensive numerical model, we examine various mixtures of N₂, CH₄, and NH₃ ices alongside dark organic compounds. While nitrogen ice remains the primary driver for both Nereid's steep redness and the neutral slopes of comparable objects, additional contributors may include specific organic impurities within the N₂ ice or particular hydrogen/carbon ratios. Unlike the moon Nereid, other objects with neutral slopes generally lack detectable methane absorption bands; thus, their similar spectral slopes likely arise from different physical mechanisms. Consequently, although Neptunian objects sharing similar spectral characteristics probably share a common bulk composition, the formation and evolutionary histories of Nereid and these other bodies appear to have diverged.

This paper introduces a novel Bayesian approach for learning dynamic treatment regimes, grounded in a robust-pessimism principle designed to mitigate the impact of distributional uncertainty inherent in outcome modeling. By leveraging closed-form full conditional posteriors for its proposed neural network priors, this method offers straightforward implementation via standard stochastic gradient Langevin algorithms. Furthermore, to enhance computational scalability for large datasets, efficient approximate Bayesian methods for approximate inference are introduced alongside a new approximate Bayesian optimization scheme for estimating posterior distributions of optimal policies. A crucial innovation in this method is a Bayesian approach to offline policy learning that explicitly accounts for unknown data distributional shifts, thereby providing robust policy recommendations. Extensive experiments using both established and custom datasets demonstrate that the proposed hierarchical deep kernel Gaussian process method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques, particularly in scenarios involving distributional uncertainty. The code will be made publicly available upon publication.

In this paper, we investigate Bogoliubov-de Gennes quasiparticles within flat band superconductors, assuming all theoretical frameworks are sound. Our findings indicate that while unpaired electrons remain stationary, Nambu fields disperse freely, forming a spectrum bounded by zero energy up to the Fermi energy ($E_F$). Consequently, we derive expressions for Green's functions and spectral functions to analyze the system's thermal and quantum thermal properties. We demonstrate that the system's thermal behavior primarily reflects the standard 3D free Fermi gas model, as the contributions from flat band superconductivity are negligible. Furthermore, we examine the critical temperature ($T_c$), finding that it is approximately equal to the cutoff energy ($E_F$) established in this study, as supported by both BCS theory and $E_F$ itself.

The generalized Polya theorem establishes that the Gaussian measure on the real line corresponds to the property equidistributing any monomial against a linear form of pairwise independent, identically distributed random variables. Our contribution generalizes this results to $L$-forms comprising variables that are $(d, \delta)$-regularly independent. Despite extending the range of applicable distributions, our methods yield significant structural insights into those possessing such regularity conditions.

Presence-absence information is prevalent in ecological data, typically indicating whether a species is found in a specific site but rarely quantifying its population size. While some researchers accept such binary data as a proxy for abundance, others argue that interpreting it solely as detection/non-detection is more accurate. Tveit and Iversen previously proposed a Bayesian network approach to analyze spatial patterns in such data, assuming no inherent link between detection probability and species abundance. Building on their work, we extend this method to incorporate population abundance information, allowing for an examination of spatial patterns whether or not abundance is present in the dataset. We also derive closed-form expressions for the correlation between abundance and presence/absence data, alongside the standard deviation of that correlation. These formulas are valid for both infinite grids and regular patterns containing an arbitrary number of species. The method is illustrated using a classic dataset concerning the spatial arrangement of seagrass *Zostera marina* and various algae.

Saliency detection aims to isolate significant objects from their backgrounds; however, challenges remain in accurately segmenting complex structures and those with intriguous backgrounds. To address these issues, we introduce a straightforward yet effective framework for Salient Object Detection (SOD) that is further supported by a newly proposed lightweight network architecture. Crucially, the framework incorporates a cross-attention context extraction module designed to broaden the detection range by aggregating contextual information from the image's periphery. Additionally, a local spatial attention mechanism is integrated into the new lightweight backbone to emphasize significant local details. For evaluation, we establish the AccSOD dataset, which includes 2,000 images sourced from the VCOl2017 benchmark, annotated with additional high-quality boundary labels. We introduce a neural architecture that mimics the computational process underlying human action perception, leveraging both spatial and motion contexts alongside intrinsic action features to enhance action recognition. By employing a progress supramodal brain area akin to the superior temporal sulcus, our model integrates these three signal types to interpret visual scenes containing multiple actors performing various movements. This study presents a model demonstrating state-of-the-art performance in action recognition tasks, validated through ablation studies that highlight the distinct contributions of spatial, motion, and intrinsic action features to this visual comprehension.

We investigate dark magnetic monopoles hypothesized to exist within a hidden $U(1)$ sector, hypothesizing that they manifest as elliptic halos formed by charged particles in equilibrium with a magnetic dipole in rotation. Observational limits imposed by the elliptical distortion of galaxies allow us to derive significant upper bounds on the mass of neutral magnetic monopoles. Specifically, if these monopoles lack any interaction with standard model particles beyond gravity, our findings restrict their mass to be below 0.55 PeV; alternatively, if they interact via any additional operator, the mass limit is tighter at 0.55 EeV. These bounds are substantially less restrictive than previous constraints derived from magnetic monopole capture by neutrino oscillillation oscillations or from a lack of muon decay anomalies associated with lepton flavor universality violations. Furthermore, we examine the implications of these monopole hypotheses for the stability of magnetic monopoles and for a specific class of axion monodromy inflation models.

This innovative architecture replaces traditional convolutional approaches with self-attention, significantly improving the accuracy of predictions across multiple future time steps. We examine an extension of the scalar electroweak theory that includes seven additional real scalars, constructed to be invariant under a $Z_2$ symmetry which has the potential to stabilize dark matter candidates. Although this model was previously analyzed in literature under the designation $3\alpha_7\beta$ (referring to its eight real scalars, $a$ to $h$), we demonstrate that it can equivalently be described using one complex scalar and five real scalars, totaling seven fields. In our re-formulation, we focus on defining the $Z_2$ symmetry through a complex scalar field $S$ and five real fields $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$. This configuration yields a set of ten distinct $Z_2$-invariant operators, enabling us to determine the relationships between the various potential functions governing the symmetry breaking. Through these findings, we elucidate the phenomenology of a first-order electroweak symmetry breaking induced by this $Z_2$ symmetry violation, exploring the resulting properties of its dark matter candidate.

Global banks sustain losses amounting to billions annually due to fraud. To detect these crimes and uncover new schemes, graph analysis is employed to decipher complex transaction patterns. This study examines these graphs within real-world transaction data by isolating and evaluating network motifs, with a specific emphasis on heterogeneous motifs given the varied nature of banking structures. We introduce a new randomization method capable of producing valid synthetic banking graphs. Findings from the exploration indicate that identifying network motifs yields both deep interpretive value and actionable insights.

This study introduces a novel, simplified approach to modeling radiation emitted from when a white dwarf star is distorted and stripped by a black hole. Rather than solving complex partial differential equations, we treat the star as remaining approximately spherically symmetric, with tidal forces inducing only minor dipole distortions calculated via perturbation theory. Under the assumption that internal pressure support aligns with the gravitational field ($\propto$), we derive analytical formulas for density and pressure distributions. Consequently, we can calculate luminosity across the electromagnetic spectrum, from radio to X-rays during the final stages of tidal disruption events (TDEs). Although aligned pressure support is a simplification, numerical tests on Polytropic models reveal this assumption yields sufficiently accurate results for electromagnetic radiation. Comparing our "1D" model against full 2D simulations shows that our method produces radiation rates that match the numerical outputs within a factor of two to three. This model offers a robust tool for rapidly generating electromagnetic spectra during TDEs, facilitating comparisons between theoretical predictions and observational data.

This study examines four variants of the symmetric Tversky ratio models proposed by Krumhuber and Tversky (2016) under the assumption that preferences are defined on three-dimensional vectors. We demonstrate that for models (A), (B), and (C), these symmetric forms fulfill the axioms of a metric when their parameters are strictly bounded. In contrast, for model (C), even with unbounded parameters, a suitable transformation of the original distance function constitutes a metric. Consequently, for all four models (A) through (D), we propose specific metric alternatives. We further present a general class of symmetric Tversay ratio formats to define distances across arbitrary multidimensional spaces and provide corresponding upper and lower bounds for each model. Our numerical evaluations include fitting procedures using simulated data across various dimensionalities as well as a multivariate analysis of real-world preference sets via maximum likelihood estimation for all four variants.

Hebbian learning refers to a theoretical framework in neuroscience where neuronal connections strengthen based on the simultaneous activation of neurons, enabling adaptive systems to refine themselves through internal processes without external guidance. This paper introduces a novel hardware implementation of a Hebbian learning rule using a resistive random-access memory (RRAM)-based crossbar architecture, demonstrating for the first time that such learning can occur entirely autonomously with no requirement for external feedback signals. By analyzing the intrinsic characteristics of this architecture-driven hebbian process, researchers have identified that the system emulates a "pulsating wave" of activity, facilitates the formation of spatial patterns among compute cells, and leads to the targeted strengthening of specific conductive pathways. Notably, studies reveal an unexpected link between this intrinsic auto-organizing behavior and "self-oscillatory" patterns, revealing a surprising synergy between autopoiesis and these patterns that mirrors self-organized spatial coherence while maintaining dynamic temporal oscillations.
